style.vernacular: Dense low-to-mid-rise International-style city: flat-roofed 2-6 storey concrete blocks and villas in sand, cream and beige painted render or stone cladding, high boundary walls round villas, glass-and-steel towers in the downtown Sharq/Salmiya skyline, co-operative society supermarkets and malls with big car parks, and sand-coloured modern mosques with a single dome and a slender minaret.
style.ornament: Pointed and multifoil arches and carved-stone or GRC screens on mosques and civic buildings; wooden or metal mashrabiya-style screens as shading; spiral blue-green enamel-disc patterns recalling mosque domes on the Kuwait Towers; sculptural spires and spheres on water towers and towers; decoration concentrated at doors and windows in older houses.

sources.what: Kuwaiti architecture: modest inward-facing traditional houses, modern International style, wooden screens, sculptural modern landmarks
hot desert climate, sparse coastal vegetation, landmarks list
spheres clad in eight shades of blue, green and grey enamelled steel discs in spiral patterns
